Row-crop opportunity — unclaimed subsidy by county

Reinsurance year 2026. Generated 2026-08-07.
opportunity
Unclaimed subsidy = eligible acres × (1 − penetration) × subsidy captured per acre. Eligible acres are acres on an individual, additional-coverage MPCI plan (YP, RP, RP-HPE, APH) — CAT acres are excluded because a CAT policy cannot carry a band at all. Penetration is that band's acres over those eligible acres. Every term is COMPUTED from RMA's Summary of Business; nothing here is an assumed rate.
Unclaimed subsidy per eligible acre = subsidy captured per acre × (1 − penetration). The same metric as the total, divided by the county's eligible acres — it strips out county SIZE, so a small county that buys nothing can outrank a big one that mostly does. A prospecting list wants the total; a "who most needs this conversation" list wants this.
Band penetration = band acres ÷ eligible acres, capped at 100%. Low penetration is where the unclaimed dollars are — but it is not a list of people who should be sold something. See the amber note below.
producer Value per acre to the PRODUCER = the federal subsidy captured on one band acre. This is the money the producer does not pay: on the RY2026 book ECO-RP captures $23.26/ac, MCO-RP $26.25/ac and SCO-RP $12.10/ac nationally, and this map shows each county's own figure. COMPUTED from Summary of Business — no rate card involved.
producer Return per producer dollar = total premium ÷ producer premium = 1 ÷ (1 − subsidy share). At FCIC's statutory target loss ratio of 1.0 (7 U.S.C. 1506(n)(2)) the expected indemnity is the whole premium, so this is what a producer dollar buys in expectation: about 5.1× on the bands. Notice how flat this map is. That flatness is the finding, not a bug — the subsidy share is set in statute, not by geography. What varies county to county is how many dollars are at stake, never how good the deal is per dollar. (Statutory expectation, not realized experience: a band's actual loss ratio in any one county in any one year will differ.)
agency Value per acre to the AGENCY = TOTAL premium per acre × your commission %. Commission is a percent of the whole premium, the subsidised portion included, which is why the agency's number keys off premium while the producer's keys off subsidy. They correlate — both scale with premium — but they are not the same ranking, because the commission rate varies by region and the subsidy share does not. ASSUMED: commission % is your own negotiated rate from data/seed/aip_commission.csv (AIP × region) or data/seed/commission_by_timezone.csv, and the values shipped there are SAMPLE data. Replace them before quoting any figure on this map.
agency Unclaimed commission = eligible acres × (1 − penetration) × TOTAL premium per acre × commission %. The prospecting number: what this county's unsold band premium is worth to your agency at your rate. ASSUMED: the commission rate — everything to the left of it is computed. The SRA's 80%-of-A&O cap on total agent compensation and RMA's schemes-or-devices rules bound real compensation and are not modelled here.
divergence Agency-minus-producer rank gap = this county's percentile under commission per acre minus its percentile under subsidy captured per acre, in percentile points. Amber = the agency is drawn here more than the producer's own interest justifies; green = the reverse, a county where the producer has more to gain than the agency has to earn. Grey is agreement. This map exists because the two rankings correlate but are not identical, and that difference is precisely where an agency's incentive and a producer's interest come apart — which is a thing to show, not to bury.
Penetration below 100% is not automatically opportunity — three things this map cannot see (expand)
Each of these makes an unsold acre legitimately unsold. (1) Election: a farm with ARC elected on a crop cannot buy SCO on that crop at all; FSA's ARC/PLC election is not in Summary of Business at any grain, so those acres are counted as eligible here and are not. (2) Basis risk: SCO, ECO and STAX trigger on a county index. A farm poorly correlated with its county gets a band that pays when it did not need it and fails to pay when it did — declining is rational, not an oversight. (Quantified separately in src/basisrisk.py.) (3) Availability: a band is only offered where the actuarial documents offer it. This page does not read ADM; it infers the offer from observed sales and grades it in the "where the band is" control.
What is modelled: SCO and STAX are mutually exclusive on the same acre, so each one's eligible acres here exclude the other's. ECO's and MCO's interactions with the others are not modelled — ECO layers above SCO by design, and MCO is in its first book year with no primary source in hand for its stacking rules. Treat this as a map of questions worth asking, not a list of people who should be sold something.
